channel.title: Daily Dose of News
channel.description: The day's most significant stories, ranked across every section.

item.title: Berlin Pride ramming suspect shot dead by police after manhunt
item.description: German police shot and killed Abdul Ballout, the 21-year-old suspect in a deadly vehicle-ramming and stabbing attack at Berlin's Christopher Street Day Pride event, ending a 24-hour manhunt on Sunday evening. Ballout, a German citizen of Lebanese heritage, was located at an allotment garden complex…

item.title: US and Iran pause strikes for second day amid diplomatic push
item.description: The United States and Iran have paused military strikes for a second consecutive day, marking the first sustained break in hostilities after nearly two weeks of nightly attacks. The relative calm comes as diplomatic efforts intensify to revive an interim ceasefire deal signed in mid-June, which has…

item.title: Israeli settlers set fire to mosques and farmland in West Bank
item.description: Israeli settlers set fire to two mosques, cars and agricultural land in the occupied West Bank overnight, Palestinian officials said, as tensions in the territory continue to escalate. item.title: Tens of thousands evacuated as wildfires rage across Europe and North Africa
item.description: Tens of thousands of people have been evacuated from their homes as wildfires continue to rage across parts of Europe and North Africa, with France and Spain among the hardest-hit countries. In France, approximately 55,000 people were evacuated overnight into Sunday from villages south of Bordeaux…

item.title: U.S. and Iran Pause Attacks, Oil Prices Drop and Stock Futures Rally
item.description: U.S. stock-index futures rallied and oil prices tumbled on Sunday as the U.S. and Iran took a pause from fighting, with Wall Street also preparing for the Federal Reserve’s meeting this week and a wave of Big Tech earnings reports, led by Apple.

item.title: Pogacar wins fifth Tour de France title amid Paris finish drama
item.description: Slovenian Tadej Pogacar won the Tour de France for a record-equalling fifth time on Sunday, crossing the line on Paris' Champs-Élysées in the peloton to join Jacques Anquetil, Eddy Merckx, Bernard Hinault and Miguel Indurain as the endurance event's most successful male riders.
